commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
[mlx] Add a pipeline for MLX builds of Grug MoE models (#10347)

Add Grug MoE conversion to 8-bit and mixed 4-bit MLX builds for Apple
Silicon, with thinking and tool calls. An artifact graph binds the
pinned source revision, prompt fixture, vLLM reference, converted model,
logprob dump, and parity report. Model file hashes and source/recipe
metadata prevent a stale dump from qualifying a different build.
Conversion links one cached download of the source into each recipe's
build and casts floating weights to bfloat16, which matches the vLLM
reference and keeps an FP32 export's unquantized weights and scales out
of FP32.

The Mac stages use a separate frozen environment pinned to mlx-lm
0.32.2. The reference stage submits an H100 job through Iris and waits
for its output; without CoreWeave credentials on the Mac, a CPU job
relays the JSON through a private Hugging Face dataset. Short prompts
and long-prompt positions beyond the sliding window have separate parity
gates. The mixed recipe keeps non-expert weights at 8 bits because a
uniform 4-bit Snowball build failed the short-case probability-error
gate.

The model file teaches mlx-lm the `<|start_think|>`/`<|end_think|>`
markers and follows vLLM's `grug` reasoning parser under
`mlx_lm.server`: thinking-mode text is reasoning once a think marker or
tool call confirms it, and an answer with neither is content. These
patches replace five mlx-lm 0.32.2 internals.

The stage scripts produced the published Snowball builds. Parity against
the Marin vLLM fork (`marin-vllm-gpu-20260924-01911be34fac`) serving
each source in bfloat16 compares top-25 logprobs at every teacher-forced
position. The gates are top-1 on decisive positions >= 0.99 and p95
probability error <= 0.075 for 8-bit, and >= 0.97 and <= 0.15 for mixed
4-bit:

| Source | Build | Short cases: top-1 decisive / p95 error | Long
prompt, positions >= 2048 |
|---|---|---|---|
| v0.1 | 8-bit | 1.000 / 0.045 | 1.000 / 0.0001 |
| v0.1 | mixed 4-bit | 0.994 / 0.100 | 1.000 / 0.0001 |
| v0.1 | uniform 4-bit, rejected | 0.978 / 0.193 | 1.000 / 0.0002 |
| v0.1.1 | 8-bit | 0.999 / 0.055 | 1.000 / 0.043 |
| v0.1.1 | mixed 4-bit | 0.994 / 0.103 | 0.997 / 0.101 |

The v0.1 long prompt repeated one paragraph for 6,148 tokens, so its
continuations stayed inside the 2,048-token window. The v0.1.1 runs use
the current fixture, 8,192 tokens of unrepeated WikiText. The v0.1.1
reference job ran in about 7 minutes on 8 H100s.

The v0.1 weights are identical to
`open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14` (39 shard
hashes), which Marin's policy evals scored on vLLM. Subsets run on the
v0.1 mixed 4-bit build at temperature 1.0 showed no capability loss:
GSM8K 0.948 on 250 items (vLLM 0.914 on the full set), MATH500 0.96 on
100 (0.962), IFBench strict 0.34 on 100 (0.300). Both v0.1 builds
recalled a fact placed at the start of the system prompt at all 8 tested
lengths from 596 to 23k tokens. `smoke_server.sh` passes on all four
published builds: thinking split, thinking off, tool call and round
trip, streamed reasoning, tool calls and unmarked answers, and a
20,491-token prompt at 3.8k–4.8k prefill and 9–12 decode tokens/s on an
M5 Max. The evals and recall checks predate the unmarked-answer parser
change, which only affects responses with no think marker.

The builds came from running the stage scripts directly. `pipeline.py`
has not yet run the full graph end to end.

Admit reused objects while the query has byte budget remaining, then

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Bound cache fills and share maintenance reads (#10573)

Cache reads return an existing local file or the backing object
location. Compaction, index backfill, table migrations, and key-bound
recovery disable cache fills and demand tracking while retaining cache
hits. Their readers use the same registered object-store backend as
queries. Compaction and migration open inputs as the merge consumes
them, preserving the decoded-memory budget; key-bound recovery reads
only footers. Immutable level promotions reuse references without
opening inputs.

Index backfill reads only the requested columns. It obtains the source
UUID from the footer and stages only the generated artifacts. It checks
existing bundles against the source UUID and row count recorded in table
state, so evicting a source file no longer triggers an index rebuild.
Cached inputs remain protected from eviction until their reads complete.
Newly written outputs still write through to the cache.

The marin hub continued downloading roughly 0.8 GiB per minute for
callers requiring complete local files after compaction stopped filling
its misses, while optional query fills remained zero. The remaining
maintenance callers now read directly from object storage on a cache
miss.

Optional query fills require a second independent request and share a
strict per-query allowance of 256 MiB and 64 objects across tables and
artifacts. Objects larger than that byte allowance remain remote
regardless of request count. Periodic request-count decay removes
entries whose counts reach zero, bounding the demand history.

Cache activity summaries report admission decisions, completed fills by
source, writes, and history pruning at most once per minute. Sweep logs
report occupancy and scan, lock-wait, and lock-hold timings; deletion
batches release the query lock between batches. The initial
cache-admission rollout's early log-read stalls remain unexplained; see
the [incident record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/854).

---------

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[grug] Balance attention work across batch shards in hero train step (#10121)

The hero train step can now permute the rows of each global batch so
that each batch shard gets a similar amount of attention work. It is off
by default and runs only when `GrugTrainerConfig.balance_attention_rows`
is set; the diagnostics launcher exposes it as
`--balance-attention-rows`. Document packing gives rows very different
attention costs, and every layer waits for the busiest shard at its next
collective. On real 16K hero batches, the busiest of 64 shards did 2.10x
the mean global-attention work.

`balance_attention_rows` counts each row's attended query-key pairs from
its FA4 segment bounds and excludes padding. It sorts the rows by this
count and deals them to the batch shards in snake order. Each shard
keeps its rows in loader order. Expert capacity drops a shard's later
tokens first, and the mixture loader shuffles rows within a batch, so
loader order spreads drops over rows of all costs. A cost order within a
shard would drop short-document rows first. A full receiver keeps
earlier senders' tokens first, so the deal starts at the shard the
costliest row was loaded on rather than at shard 0. Context ranks share
rows, so the shard count excludes the context axis. With one row per
shard, as in the 262K CP4 layout, placement cannot change any shard's
work, so the batch is returned unchanged. The count is at token
granularity. FA4 skips whole 128x128 tiles, so rows of short documents
cost somewhat more than counted. With this count, the busiest-to-mean
ratio at 16K falls from 2.10 to 1.17 for global layers and from 1.46 to
1.05 for local layers. These ratios were computed before padding was
excluded from the count.

Every token still enters the loss and the router statistics. Row
placement changes which assignments exceed expert capacity, so the loss
changes slightly.

Each pair of arms ran on one GB200 NVL72 rack. The step-time change is
the median per-step paired difference with a 95% bootstrap interval.

| Context | Mesh and batch | Restored from | Control s/step | Balanced
s/step | Step time | Scored steps |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 65K | CP4 x EP16, 64 rows | hero-ctx16k-step257k, step 300000 | 15.352
| 14.743 | -3.63% [-4.02, -2.85] | 106 / 57 |
| 16K | EP64, 256 rows | hero-mfu30-step231k, step 240000 | 13.134 |
13.078 | -0.40% [-0.46, -0.31] | 106 / 106 |

The balanced 65K arm was preempted once, so only 57 steps are paired.
The drop fraction rises by about 0.5% at both lengths (ratio 1.006 at
65K, 1.005 at 16K). The only same-code A/A pair is at 16K: its loss
difference has an RMS of 4.5e-4 and a maximum of 1.4e-3. The 65K loss
difference is inside that band (RMS 2.6e-4, maximum 1.9e-3). The 16K
loss difference is above it (RMS 8.3e-4, maximum 5.8e-3, mean +2.8e-4).
No 65K A/A pair exists.

The permutation all-gathers the whole global batch to every GPU: 12
bytes per global token for the tokens, the loss weights and the q
segment ids, which also serve as the kv ids. At the 11-rack 65K layout
of 704 rows, that is about 0.55 GB per GPU per step. The cost of this
gather across racks has not been measured. Balancing is therefore
opt-in: it gained 3.6% at 65K but only 0.4% at 16K on one rack, and at
16K on 11 racks the gather may cost a large share of that gain. The 65K
hero switch is expected to turn it on.

LOOM_CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN Secret Manager secret, which holds a
one-year
token from `claude setup-token`. Claude sessions previously relied on
the
interactive login stored on the session home volume that every session
shares,
and they signed out whenever that login lapsed.

The token goes to the interactive profiles, which accept a per-launch
agent
override, and to the pr-review, pr-holistic-review, and pm Claude
profiles.
Strict Codex profiles cannot run Claude and do not receive it. Loom
resolves
versions/latest at each agent start, so rotation needs only a new secret
version.

The stack now imports each secret that a profile references, currently
the
Claude token and LOOM_PM_BOARD_TOKEN. Pulumi tracks the secrets but
never a
version, so values stay out of Pulumi state. A reference to a missing
secret
fails preview, and removing the last reference retains the secret. The
VM
account's project-level Secret Manager accessor grant covers every
reference.

[infra] Drop the root uv version floor that breaks older task images (#10583)

The root project no longer sets uv's `required-version`. Iris task setup
runs `uv sync` with the uv in the cluster's task image, and clusters
started before #10574 ship uv 0.12.3. With the `>=0.13.5` floor added in
#10580, task setup on those clusters stops with:

```
error: Required uv version `>=0.13.5` does not match the running version `0.12.3`.
```

uv 0.12.3 reads the current lock without changes. Marin's images and
SkyRL install uv 0.13.5 themselves, and CI's setup-uv installs the

older installs keep uv's previous bundled roots until they upgrade.

Co-authored-by: rjpower <rjpower@users.noreply.github.com>

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[infra] Remove the eMudhra root from uv, Node, and third-party images (#10580)

Marin's uv, Node, CI, and third-party images no longer trust the
compromised eMudhra (emSign) CA.
[CVE-2026-111943](https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/10/20/1)
covers eight intermediates under `emSign ECC Root CA - G3` whose private
keys are recoverable from their certificates. #10574 rebuilt Marin's own
images; this change covers the tools and images around them.

uv is now 0.13.5 in the project requirements, install scripts, and
TaskTrove's generated Dockerfiles. That release drops the root from uv's
bundled store and rejects chains that contain any of the eight
intermediate keys. Relocking the root project under 0.13.5 rewrote about
640 lines of environment markers into an equivalent normalized form. The
SkyRL, Harbor, and Evalchemy locks move to certifi 2026.10.23 and grpcio
1.84.1. `marin-iris` now requires the first `marin-iris-native` wheel
built with webpki-roots 1.0.11.

CI and images move to Node 24. Node 20 is end of life and has no fixed
release, while Node 24.22.1 updates its bundled roots. CI sets
`check-latest` because hosted runners cache older Node 24 builds. The
TPU CI VMs reset daily and pick up the rebuilt image.

Three pinned third-party images ship stale stores, and their tags are
not rebuilt upstream. Each now refreshes its own store:

- Harbor's `docker:28.3.3-dind` runs `apk upgrade ca-certificates` in
both the Daytona and Modal builds.
- The TEI task setup installs the current `ca-certificates` from the
Ubuntu archive.
- The Open-MOPD image refreshes the OS store and certifi, points gRPC at
the OS store, and replaces uv 0.8.22.

Loom's Caddy moves to 2.11.7, whose image already has a clean store. It
takes effect on the next Loom infrastructure deploy.

Some exposure remains:

- The NeMo-Skills sandbox image is unchanged because it runs with
network access denied.
- Existing TaskTrove archives keep their uv 0.8 Dockerfiles until they
are reconverted.
- openai-harmony and wandb's bundled parquet library still embed the
root, and neither project has a fixed release.
- The Open-MOPD build script sources a Kaniko helper that was never
vendored, so no new image can be built until it is restored.

The Loom image changes are in marin-community/loom#407.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[infra] Remove the compromised eMudhra CA from container trust stores (#10574)

Rebuilt Iris, Finelog, Marina, and Grafana images no longer trust
certificates from the eight eMudhra (emSign) intermediate CAs whose
private keys were found to be recoverable from their public certificates
([CVE-2026-111943](https://www.openwall.com/lists/oss-security/2026/10/20/1),
which lists them). The intermediates chain to `emSign ECC Root CA - G3`,
and Sectigo's `AAA Certificate Services` (`Comodo AAA Services root` in
Debian) cross-signed them. Mozilla removed the G3 root from NSS on
2026-10-20. Debian's `ca-certificates` 20250419~deb12u2 (bookworm) and
20250419+deb13u1 (trixie) remove both roots.

The images published before this change trust the compromised chain
through several stores. Each version in the last column drops the
affected roots:

| Trust store | Published state | Fixed by |
|---|---|---|
| OS `ca-certificates` | Old store in `finelog:latest` (built
2026-10-18), the 2026-10-22 `iris-worker`, and the
`grafana/grafana:13.1.1-ubuntu` base | Image builds pass `--pull`. The
Grafana Dockerfile installs `ca-certificates`, which upgrades the copy
in its pinned base image. |
| Rust `webpki-roots` in `finelog-server` (TLS to the Finelog hub) and
`iris_native` (Iris proxy client) | Embeds the G3 root | webpki-roots
1.0.11, rustls-webpki 0.103.16 |
| uv binary | 0.12.3 in Iris and Marina, 0.9.7 in Grafana | uv 0.13.5 |
| Google Cloud SDK bundles in the Iris controller and worker | 590.0.0
bundles both roots | `google-cloud-cli` 590.0.1, pinned |
| grpcio `roots.pem` | 1.76.0 in Iris, 1.82.1 in Grafana | grpcio 1.84.1
|
| Grafana bridge certifi | 2026.6.17 | certifi 2026.10.23 |

The 2026-10-22 worker image had trixie's unpatched `ca-certificates`
20250419, although a `python:3.12-slim` with 20250419+deb13u1 was
published on 2026-10-21. Docker's default build driver uses the
builder's local copy of a base image without checking the registry. The
Iris build also reads layers from its registry build cache, so every
layer built on that stale base is reused. The Iris and Finelog build
commands now pass `--pull`, and every Pulumi image build (Cloud Run,
Finelog on Kubernetes, Loom, Shellsim) sets `pull=True`. Both resolve
base tags against the registry. The same cache keeps the gcloud install
layer while the base image and command are unchanged, so an unpinned
install keeps 590.0.0. The pin changes the command and forces 590.0.1.

rustls-webpki 0.103.16 adds a blocklist that rejects any chain
containing one of the compromised intermediate public keys, so
cross-signed copies are rejected too. webpki-roots 1.0.11 also drops
`emSign Root CA - C1` and `emSign ECC Root CA - C3`, following Mozilla's
removal of both. The Iris Dockerfile now names the uv image once, so the
next uv bump is one edit.

Some bundles in the rebuilt images still contain an affected root:

- pip 25.0.1 from the Python base image vendors an old certifi, but pip
verifies through the patched system store by default. botocore and
httplib2 ship their own bundles, but they load certifi, which the images
install at 2026.10.19 or later.
- Marina installs `iris_native` from the PyPI `marin-iris-native` wheel,
which still embeds the G3 root. `marin-release-libs-wheels.yaml`
publishes a new wheel when this change merges. Bumping
`marin-iris-native` in `uv.lock` afterwards picks it up.
- The Loom image builds from the `marin-community/loom` repository,
whose lock pins webpki-roots 1.0.7 and rustls-webpki 0.103.15 and whose
gcloud install is unpinned. It needs the same bumps there.
- `openai-harmony` 0.0.8 and `wandb` 0.26.0 embed the G3 root in their
Rust extensions. Neither project has released since the incident, so
these stay until upstream ships fixes.

Running services keep the old images until they are redeployed. Merging
redeploys Grafana and Marina through the Pulumi rollout workflow. Iris
needs `iris cluster controller restart` on each cluster; it builds the
controller and task images, plus the worker image on VM clusters.
Finelog needs a rebuild and deploy through `finelog build-image` or the
`infra/finelog` stack. This change does not touch the legacy
`levanter-base` image, last built on 2026-06-21; it needs a manual
rebuild if it is still in use.

commits.author: rjpower
commits.message:
[finelog] Bound cache warming and release readers during cleanup (#10552)

Limit optional object-cache warming to immediately available download
slots. Broad or cancelled queries previously left queued fills
downloading and writing objects long after the request ended, competing
with ingestion and repeatedly evicting cached data.

Release the shared query-visibility lock between batches of 16 cache
removals, including object garbage collection. Keep each batch's
write-lock guard inside its blocking task, which can continue after its
caller is cancelled, so readers cannot overlap an unfinished unlink.
Readers retain their existing protection against files disappearing
during a scan.

One Marin hub log request spent 12.05 seconds waiting for this lock and
0.56 seconds querying. A cache sweep removed 28,535 files under one
write lock. The change bounds concurrent cache warming and limits each
cleanup lock acquisition to 16 removals without changing stored data,
retention, or deployment resource limits. Incident:
https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/843.

commits.author: dlwh
commits.message:
[grug] Add GB200 launch and H100 validation support (#9662)

Add a GB200 launcher, tracked JAXPP runtime overlay and fresh Harrier
data support to the H100 pipeline foundation merged in #9279. The
launcher requests one NVLink domain in the opportunistic batch queue,
separates admission and execution deadlines, and disables failure and
preemption retries. Fresh-data trials explicitly disable simulated
epoching, preserving full datasets even when the mixture schedule
exceeds the simulated-token budget. The diagnostic fetches one batch at
a time on demand, closes its iterators, and uses the same
batch-placement policy for compilation and training. Checkpoint metadata
includes the data source, seed, schedule horizon and router-bias
adaptation mode.

The runtime pins JAXPP `328f75a80cecf22c7cc030a82d8941d3c1e220b6` plus
`runtime/jaxpp_host_startup.patch` (SHA256
`d987c16ece399fe5eeb69d413703d549135635f19a57dc4b6c60cc0d1ea4b1a7`),
which keeps activation copies in forward tasks, preserves pinned-host
output placement and warms tasks with disposable inputs. JAX 0.11.1
overrides JAXPP's declared compatibility cap and remains experimental.
The overlay installer prevents Git from silently skipping files inside a
repository-local virtual environment. Installer recovery avoids
duplicate global reinstall flags; the [incident
record](https://marina.oa.dev/echo/wiki/600) distinguishes the initial
GitHub fetch failure from the recovery-command failure.

At executable `0da04acccf7b0842319a8668d71ccc697a7b10ec`, the
eight-GB200 synthetic gate completed two finite updates with losses
11.806337356567383 and 0.4912489652633667. All eight native processes,
both GPU tasks and the coordinator exited zero; all 48 startup task ABI
records had zero input memory-kind mismatches. At
`a1e3ab278eeb05bb645db641dd3e7dabedf90dbb`, 16 H100s completed ten
synthetic and twenty fresh-data updates, consuming 2,621,440 fresh
tokens with all 200 components nonempty. Both gates used two width-6144
layers from the [Hero model
recipe](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/hero-gb200-pipeline/experiments/grug/moe_hero_ep/hero_recipe.py)
and FP32 parameters with BF16 compute. The H100 adapter uses
pooled-wave/FA4 transport with SYRK disabled and establishes no
ragged-transport parity. [GB200
commands](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/hero-gb200-pipeline/experiments/grug/moe_hero_pipeline/GB200.md)
and the [H100
reference](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/hero-gb200-pipeline/docs/references/hero-pipeline-h100.md)
retain runtime details and acceptance criteria.

The hardware gates predate the merged foundation's expert-bank
normalization correction and option to freeze the adaptive router bias.
The reconciled branch has not been rerun on GPUs. GPU checkpoint
evidence remains limited to the [historical reduced-model
comparison](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/codex/hero-gb200-pipeline/docs/references/hero-pipeline-h100.md#checkpoint-boundary-and-storage)
at `77b4b15cae978b9acf2a721c47c3606773f6a177`: 90,018,826 stored bytes
and a resumed-versus-uninterrupted loss difference of 9.5367431640625e-7
within unchanged 1e-5 tolerances. Full 48-layer main-recipe execution
and GPU checkpoint continuation on the reconciled branch remain
unvalidated; the 64-GB200 rack attempt failed during installation before
any finite updates.

Co-authored-by: Matt Wittmann <matt.wittmann@openathena.ai>
